A pair of head/tail pointers, maintaining a list of intrusive nodes.

Intrusive nodes do not need separate allocations for the links, but store them in the linked objects, in the MP member. The main thing this class does is to compute the address of the object by subtracting the offset from the address of the member storing the pointers.

For statically allocated lists, set L=<Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/static-double-list-links">static&#95;double&#95;list&#95;links</Link>.

### initialize_once() {#a6ea6345b2ce0664b1fc1bbd484d7a653}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class N, N T::* MP, class L, class U&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>void micro_os_plus::utils::intrusive_list&lt; T, N, MP, L, U &gt;::initialize_once (void)</>}>
Initialize the list only at first run.

<SectionUser title="Parameters">
None.
</SectionUser>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Nothing.
</SectionUser>

If the statically allocated list is still in the initial <em>uninitialised</em> state (with both pointers null), initialise the list to the empty state, with both pointers pointing to itself.

For non-statically initialised lists, this method is ineffective.

:::info
Must be manually called for statically allocated list before inserting elements, or any other operations.
:::

### links_ {#a22d5f70c0589acc1c18d10e740c7a599}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class N, N T::* MP, class L, class U&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>links_type micro_os_plus::utils::double_list&lt; N, double_list_links &gt;::links_</>}
 labels = {["protected"]}>
The list top node used to point to <b>head</b> and <b>tail</b> nodes.

The node <b>next</b> pointer points to the list head, and the <b>previous</b> pointer points to the list tail.

To simplify processing, the list always has these pointers set, with an empty list node pointing to itself.
